summary: A ten-segment bar for a value against a known ceiling.

pairs.dont: Show a meter on its own and expect it to carry the value.
pairs.do: Always pair it with the number it represents.
pairs.why: It moves in 20% steps, so it cannot tell you 3.4 from 3.9 — and it is hidden from screen readers, so on its own it says nothing at all.

pairs.dont: Use a meter for something that is completing — an upload, an import.
pairs.do: Use Progress for work in flight; a meter is for a reading.
pairs.why: Progress implies an end state and a direction. A meter is a measurement that can go back down.

pairs.dont: Use a meter for an unbounded number like calls per hour.
pairs.do: Use it where the maximum is real and known — MOS out of 5, a score out of 100.
pairs.why: The bar is a fraction of something. With an invented ceiling, the fill is an opinion rather than a measurement.

pairs.dont: Draw an empty-looking meter when there is no reading.
pairs.do: Pass status unknown, so nothing lights and the value reads "—".
pairs.why: A meter at zero says the measurement is zero. No reading and a reading of nothing are different facts.
